transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-14
- Time: 10:00 AM PT
- Duration: 45m
- Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Nina Patel, Carlos Ruiz, Emily Wong (AstraHealth)

Summary (auto): review of weekly benchmarks comparing Redwood runtime to customer's baseline provider. Focus on latency distribution, throughput at scale, and tuning knobs (batching, quantization, KV cache).

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick checkin, uh we have the latest numbers from the bench, i'll give a 5 min high level then liam will walk the traces
00:18 Speaker 2 (Nina): great, thanks maya, we only have the core infra folks today, carlos emily, we'll put product folks on next week if needed
00:28 Speaker 3 (Liam): alright so main takeaway, for the 2k qps sim the redwood setup delivered ~95ms p50 vs baseline ~180ms p50, p95 was ~230ms vs baseline 420ms, p99 traces show some tail from network jitter on the baseline runs
00:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): yeah and important note, we ran redwood with the small-batch continuous batching profile and enabled 4-bit quantization (llm-q4_0) on the test nodes, baseline was running fp16 on their provider
01:05 Speaker 2 (Carlos): sorry can you repeat the p95 numbers? i might've missed that
01:09 Speaker 3 (Liam): p95 redwood ~230ms, baseline ~420ms, and p99 redwood ~560ms but baseline had p99 spikes beyond 1.2s on a few runs
01:25 Speaker 2 (Nina): okay that delta is interesting; what's the throughput comparison at 95th? like sustained tokens/sec?
01:33 Speaker 3 (Liam): sustained tokens per second, redwood ~11k tps across the pool, baseline ~8.5k tps. that maps to roughly 30% better token throughput for the same instance count in our bench config
01:50 Speaker 4 (Emily): curious about warm start vs cold start - our prod traffic has big diurnal changes and we worry about cold starts on the nightly scale-downs
02:02 Speaker 3 (Liam): good question - we measured cold-start latency: cold-boot (cold cache, node spin-up) adds ~800ms for redwood vs baseline ~1.6s, but once a node is hot KV cache warmup makes p50 drop to the 80-100ms window
02:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): also worth flagging our smart routing falls back to a cheaper model variant automatically which can avoid hard OOMs; in your config we didn't run fallback but it's available
02:32 Speaker 2 (Carlos): what's the memory/kv size for your test runs? our model has a large kv footprint because of long-context sessions
02:40 Speaker 3 (Liam): we used a 48GB KV allotment per shard, sequence length distribution averaged 1k tokens. for longer contexts we recommended splitting across shards and enabling prefix cache, that cut p50 by ~15% in followup tests
03:02 Speaker 4 (Emily): any issues with tokenization mismatch? baseline uses slightly different tknr, we saw token counts vary 3-4% which affected cost calc
03:15 Speaker 1 (Maya): yeah tokenizer differences can bias the token-per-invocation math; we'll normalize in the sheet, liam will include raw tokens and normalized tokens columns
03:30 Speaker 2 (Nina): what about security, if we go private, can we keep audit logs in our KMS and still use the redwood control plane?
03:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, private deployment supports customer KMS and audit log ingestion; we'll send the SOC2 + network topology docs after the call
03:54 Speaker 2 (Carlos): cost, quick question: dedicated vs hosted, for our commit level (est 10M tokens/mo) what's the delta? roughly 20-25%?
04:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): rough rule of thumb, dedicated reserved pools target 15-35% lower unit cost depending on commit and autoscale behavior; we'll put a modeled estimate in the sheet for your numbers
04:18 Speaker 3 (Liam): back to perf - we noticed the baseline provider had higher tail when their autoscaler was spinning up new instances during the spike scenarios, that manifested as queued requests and p99 spikes
04:32 Speaker 2 (Nina): do you have the raw traces for that? we'd like to see timeline and thread dumps if possible
04:40 Speaker 3 (Liam): yes, i captured the raw traces; some of the spikes align with GC events on the baseline side and network reshuffling — we attached the timeline CSV in the shared drive link (link: https://redwood-internal.example/bench/astro-10-14)
04:58 Speaker 4 (Emily): the KV cache warmup script - can that be turned into a crontab or kubernetes job? we don't want manual steps
05:06 Speaker 3 (Liam): yep we wrote a small warmup script that replays common prefixes, we'll add a k8s job example and an init container pattern to the repo
05:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): another thing, we tested quantization at q4_0 and q5_1; q5_1 maintained quality better but slightly higher latency, q4_0 was most cost efficient for your tolerance
05:35 Speaker 2 (Carlos): how was eval quality measured? human eval or automated metrics? we care about hallucination and F1 on our IE tasks
05:43 Speaker 3 (Liam): automated metrics (BLEU/F1) on your provided eval set; next cycle we'll run a small human eval on a 200-sample slice to confirm; initial numbers looked within <2% of baseline on F1 for extraction tasks
06:00 Speaker 2 (Nina): can we push a stress run with 5k sustained qps to see autoscaler behavior? we'd like to test failure modes too
06:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we can schedule a staged stress test; we'll provide a harness and synthetic traffic pumper, liam will own the test config
06:18 Speaker 4 (Emily): minor note - our corporate firewall requires TLS mutual auth for inbound, is that supported for private?
06:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes mTLS supported for private deployments; we'll include the connection checklist in the docs pack
06:33 Speaker 2 (Carlos): any concerns about vendor lock if we move to dedicated? we want portability in case we switch providers
06:41 Speaker 3 (Liam): portability is a design goal; you can pin model versions and we provide exportable manifest and init scripts so you can rehydrate workloads elsewhere if needed
06:52 Speaker 2 (Nina): ok let's quick recap of owners and dates
07:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap: maya will send the full benchmark CSV + p99 traces by 10/16, liam will add kv warmup k8s job + repo link by 10/18, emily will run staging stress tests by 10/20 and post logs, carlos provide prod prompt set by 10/17; plan on on-prem deep dive week of 10/26 if staging goes well
07:28 Speaker 4 (Emily): thanks all, that timeline works, i'll coordinate with infra to run the harness tomorrow evening
07:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): great, thanks everyone, end of call

Notes:
- Shared artifacts: https://redwood-internal.example/bench/astro-10-14 (benchmark CSV + traces), link to SOC2 and private deploy checklist will be added to the folder
- Observations: Redwood's continuous batching + 4-bit quantization gave ~30% throughput uptick and ~2x improvement in p95 vs baseline in these tests; p99 tail still needs more gating under large burst scenarios
